channel.title: Zone3 — Air Fryer Research Desk
channel.description: Question-shaped air-fryer guides, comparisons and research articles, each claim linked to the official page it came from. As an Amazon Associate we earn from qualifying purchases.

item.title: What “4-in-1” actually names — and what a listing leaves out
item.description: Counted claims read closely, the temperature that is worth checking, and a two-minute test you can run on any listing.

item.title: Dual-basket vs single-basket: which layout suits how you cook?
item.description: Two 3QT baskets are not one 6QT with a divider — what the layout changes at dinnertime, and when the single big basket wins.

item.title: Which air fryer parts actually go in the dishwasher — checked line by line
item.description: The claim is about a basket, not a machine. What each listing states, and the one place the care section beats the title.

item.title: 6QT, 8QT and 26QT: what the capacity numbers do and do not tell you
item.description: The quart figures quoted from each listing, the ratios shown as our arithmetic, and the four checks to run before you pick.

item.title: Air fryer oven vs basket fryer: the 26QT is not a bigger basket
item.description: What doors, a convection cavity and six included accessories change — and why Amazon files this machine under Air Fryers, not Air Fryer Ovens.

item.title: What Sync Finish actually does — and who a dual-basket fryer is for
item.description: Sync Finish on a dual-basket air fryer explained: what the CHEFMAN listing states, what it does not, and how to tell whether the two-basket layout fits your kitchen.

item.title: 450°F Hi-Fry: what the listings promise, and what they leave out
item.description: Two air fryer listings name the same Hi-Fry feature; only one states a temperature. What a high-heat finish setting is for, and how to read air-fryer titles literally.

item.title: French-door air fryer ovens: five questions before you choose the 26-quart format
item.description: The Emeril Lagasse 26QT French Door listing states 24 presets, convection cooking and six included accessories. Five questions to decide whether the oven format fits your kitchen.

item.title: How to read an Amazon listing title like a buyer
item.description: Sixty characters of marketing, written to be skimmed. Five habits that turn a title into actual information.

item.title: How this site gets paid, and what that does to the copy
item.description: The commission rate, the click window, the payment lag and the rules about which numbers we are even allowed to print. No vague 'we may earn a commission'. Actual terms.

item.title: French doors, Sync Finish and a 450°F button
item.description: Three listings, twenty-odd named features, and one honest category: the ones that change what you can cook, and the ones that just change the price of the word 'multi'.

item.title: 'Dishwasher-safe' describes a part, not a machine
item.description: All three listings promise it. None of them promises what most people mean by it. Here is the exact wording, and the two questions to ask instead.

item.title: 6 QT, 8 QT and 26 QT are not the same kind of number
item.description: Quartage is the first thing printed on an air fryer listing and the least useful thing to compare. Here is the arithmetic the box skips, using three real listings.

item.title: One of these three is on Amazon's best-seller list today
item.description: Not the one most people would guess. What the list is, what a rank means on the day you read it, and why we publish the date.

item.title: Where air fryers sit in Amazon's category tree - and why the category decides the commission
item.description: One breadcrumb, one row of a public rate table: how the 4.50% Kitchen rate attaches to the three listings this site tracks, and when the money actually arrives.

item.title: What you can say about a product you have not used
item.description: The FTC's one-line rule on experience claims, Amazon's accuracy clause, and the editorial standard this desk follows instead of fake hands-on reviews.

item.title: What an Amazon affiliate link has to look like - and why a short link can earn nothing
item.description: The tag rule, the link-shortener rule and the redirect rule, read from Amazon's own policy pages - plus the audit this project ran on the three links it was handed.

item.title: The 24-hour window: how Amazon's shopping session actually pays
item.description: 24 hours, 89 days, 180 days - the three clocks inside every qualifying purchase, read from the Commission Income Statement, plus the things that quietly cancel a commission.
